publisher: U.S. Government Publishing Office (Public Laws 115-97, 117-2 and 119-21); Internal Revenue Service (Revenue Procedure 2025-32)
title_or_table: Public Law 115-97, sec. 11022; Public Law 117-2, sec. 9611; Public Law 119-21, sec. 70104; Rev. Proc. 2025-32, sec. 3.05, Child Tax Credit
universe_or_base: The maximum child tax credit per qualifying child that the law sets for each tax year, before phase-outs and refundability limits
vintage: Statute texts on govinfo.gov and Rev. Proc. 2025-32 as read on November 11, 2026
qualification: The maximum credit is not what every family receives: income limits, phase-outs, the refundable cap ($1,400 indexed under Public Law 115-97, $1,700 for 2025 and 2026) and, from 2025, the Social Security number rules decide each family's amount. In 2021 the credit was fully refundable and $3,600 for a child under 6. The 2017 value of $1,000 is the base amount in 26 U.S.C. 24(a) that Public Law 115-97 replaced, read from that law's text

max_credit_per_child.description: maximum credit per qualifying child 6 or older (every qualifying child outside 2021)

max_credit_young_child.description: maximum credit for a child under 6

law.description: the law that set the amount

Retrieved November 11, 2026. The maximum before income limits and refundability caps.
